title: Signed total tensor and both K-flat tests under an exact monoidal equivalence
statement:
Let $\mathcal M,\mathcal A$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian] with symmetric monoidal structures [def-sfb-monoidal-category], each with a symmetry $\beta_{X,Y}:X\otimes Y\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\otimes X$ natural in both variables, with $\beta_{Y,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y}=\mathrm{id}$ and the hexagon identity $\alpha_{Y,Z,X}\circ\beta_{X,Y\otimes Z}\circ\alpha_{X,Y,Z}=(\mathrm{id}_Y\otimes\beta_{X,Z})\circ\alpha_{Y,X,Z}\circ(\beta_{X,Y}\otimes\mathrm{id}_Z)$, whose tensors are additive in each variable and preserve countable coproducts in each variable. Let $F:\mathcal M\to\mathcal A$ be an additive exact equivalence, with additive exact quasi-inverse $G$, and a specified strong monoidal structure [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Write its inverse tensorator as $c_{X,Y}:F(X\otimes Y)\cong FX\otimes FY$, and assume it is symmetric: $c_{Y,X}\circ F(\beta_{X,Y})=\beta_{FX,FY}\circ c_{X,Y}$ for all $X,Y$. Use integer cochain complexes, cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]: $(P\otimes Q)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n}P^p\otimes Q^q$, with differential $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^p1\otimes d_Q$. Assume these countable coproducts exist in both categories. Flat means that tensor with the object is exact; acyclic means that every cohomology object is zero; the acyclic-test K-flat condition means that total tensor with every acyclic complex is acyclic.
The termwise functors $F_{\rm Ch},G_{\rm Ch}$ preserve and reflect acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms. There is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\tau_{P,Q}:F_{\rm Ch}\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Tot}(F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes F_{\rm Ch}Q),$$
whose component on each $(p,q)$ summand is $c_{P^p,Q^q}$ followed by that summand's coproduct injection, using the canonical coproduct comparison for $F$. It respects the signed differential, associators, both unitors and the Koszul symmetry $(-1)^{pq}\beta$ on homogeneous bidegree $(p,q)$, and $G_{\rm Ch}$ has the inverse comparison. For every object $M$ and complex $P$,
$$M\text{ is flat}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ FM\text{ is flat},\qquad P\text{ is acyclic-test K-flat}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ F_{\rm Ch}P\text{ is acyclic-test K-flat}.$$
In each category this K-flat condition is equivalent to requiring both total tensor functors with $P$ to preserve every quasi-isomorphism, with arbitrary endpoints. Thus $F_{\rm Ch}$ and $G_{\rm Ch}$ also preserve and reflect the two-sided quasi-isomorphism-test K-flat condition of [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso].

source.place: Tag 06YP, lemma-K-flat-quasi-isomorphism; agent-written abstract exact-equivalence and signed-total version of the cone argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to $F$ and $G$. It gives natural isomorphisms $H^n(F_{\rm Ch}P)\cong F(H^nP)$ and $H^n(G_{\rm Ch}K)\cong G(H^nK)$. An additive equivalence reflects zero objects: if $FT=0$, then $\mathrm{id}_T$ maps to zero and hence is zero by faithfulness, so $T$ is a zero object. It also reflects invertibility: apply the quasi-inverse and conjugate with the unit. Thus both termwise functors preserve and reflect acyclicity and quasi-isomorphisms, in every integer degree.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor; natural cohomology comparison of the cited node

proof.text: Choose the adjoint-equivalence unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\cong GF$ and counit $\epsilon:FG\cong\mathrm{id}$ (an equivalence may be expressed as an adjoint equivalence). By [lem-galois-equivalence-preserves-limits], $F$ and $G$ preserve all existing coproducts, in particular those indexed by $\{(p,q):p+q=n\}\cong\mathbf Z$. Give $G$ the strong monoidal structure of [lem-sfb-monoidal-equivalence-inverse-structure], and write $c^G=(\mu^G)^{-1}$. Its four equations specify the inverse comparison relative to $\eta,\epsilon$. This uses only the given monoidal structures, not a transported replacement for either category.

Write $\iota_{p,q}$ for the degree-$n$ coprojections of $P\otimes Q$ and $\iota'_{p,q}$ for those of $FP\otimes FQ$. Since $(F\operatorname{Tot}^n,F\iota_{p,q})$ is a coproduct, its universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] defines the unique map $\tau^n$ with $\tau^n F(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}c_{P^p,Q^q}$. The reverse coproduct map is specified by $F(\iota_{p,q})c_{P^p,Q^q}^{-1}$. Each composite is identity on every coprojection, hence is identity. These are precisely the canonical coproduct comparison composed with the coproduct of the inverse tensorators. All these indexing sets are countable.

The chain-map identity is checked after $F(\iota_{p,q})$. Additivity of $F$ and naturality of $c$ give on both sides the same map
$$\iota'_{p+1,q}(F(d_P^p)\otimes1)c_{P^p,Q^q}+(-1)^p\iota'_{p,q+1}(1\otimes F(d_Q^q))c_{P^p,Q^q}.$$
Here $F((-1)^pa)=(-1)^pF(a)$, also for negative $p$. Thus the degreewise inverse maps assemble to a chain isomorphism. For chain maps $a:P\to P'$, $b:Q\to Q'$, naturality is the equation $c_{P'^p,Q'^q}F(a^p\otimes b^q)=(Fa^p\otimes Fb^q)c_{P^p,Q^q}$ on each coprojection. This proves naturality of $\tau$ in both arguments.

The ordinary total-complex associator is induced on a triple summand by $\alpha_{P^p,Q^q,R^r}$, reindexing the two nested sums over $p+q+r=n$. Tensor preserves these countable coproducts. It is a chain map since either parenthesization has differential with the three coefficients $1,(-1)^p,(-1)^{p+q}$. Its inverse is induced by $\alpha^{-1}$. The pentagon and triangle reduce on quadruple and triple summands to their defining equations in [def-sfb-monoidal-category]; all the relevant finite powers of $\mathbf Z$ are countable. Unit objects are $\mathbf1[0]$, and the unitors are induced by $\lambda,\rho$ on the sole potentially nonzero summands $(0,n),(n,0)$; tensor with a zero object is zero since an additive functor sends its identity to zero.

Test the two associativity composites for $\tau$ on each nested triple coprojection. By naturality past the inner coprojection their equality becomes exactly
$$(1\otimes c_{Y,Z})c_{X,Y\otimes Z}F(\alpha_{X,Y,Z})=\alpha_{FX,FY,FZ}(c_{X,Y}\otimes1)c_{X\otimes Y,Z},$$
which is the inverse-tensorator form of the associativity equation in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. For the unit comparison take $j:F(\mathbf1)[0]\cong\mathbf1[0]$ to be $e_F^{-1}$ in degree zero and the zero-object isomorphisms elsewhere. On $(0,n)$ and $(n,0)$ the two unitor equalities reduce respectively to
$$F(\lambda_X)=\lambda_{FX}(e_F^{-1}\otimes1)c_{\mathbf1,X},\quad F(\rho_X)=\rho_{FX}(1\otimes e_F^{-1})c_{X,\mathbf1}.$$
These are the two unit axioms in the cited definition, with the structure maps inverted. Coproduct uniqueness proves the required equalities of complexes.

The signed symmetry $b_{P,Q}$ has summand map $(-1)^{pq}\beta_{P^p,Q^q}$ into $(q,p)$. It commutes with differentials: for the $d_P$ term the two exponents are $pq+q=(p+1)q$, and for the $d_Q$ term they are $pq$ and $p+p(q+1)$, equal modulo $2$. The reverse signed swap is its inverse since $pq+qp$ is even and $\beta_{Y,X}\beta_{X,Y}=1$. Its hexagon follows on triple summands from $p(q+r)=pq+pr$ and the assumed hexagon for $\beta$. On each $(p,q)$ summand the symmetry compatibility of $\tau$ reduces to
$$(-1)^{pq}c_{Q^q,P^p}F(\beta_{P^p,Q^q})=(-1)^{pq}\beta_{FP^p,FQ^q}c_{P^p,Q^q},$$
which is the stated symmetric-functor hypothesis; additivity allows the sign to pass through $F$. Thus $\tau$ respects the Koszul symmetry as well as the constraints already checked.

The forward tensor and unit comparisons of steps 3-7 define a strong monoidal structure on the termwise functor of the equivalence of cochain complexes. Apply [lem-sfb-monoidal-equivalence-inverse-structure] directly to this equivalence of complexes, with the existing signed-total monoidal structures on both categories. Its canonical inverse structure supplies the inverse tensor and unit comparisons, their naturality, associativity and unitor equations, and the four required equations for the termwise unit and counit. Its braiding compatibility follows by faithfulness of the forward functor: postcompose its image with the forward tensor comparison and the tensor product of the counit components. The counit tensor equation reduces both sides to counit naturality and the forward braiding equation proved in step 7. Cancel these isomorphisms. This avoids repeating the summand construction for the inverse, while using the specified termwise unit and counit unchanged.

For an object $M$ the functor $FM\otimes-$ is naturally isomorphic to $F\circ(M\otimes-)\circ G$: the comparison at $N$ is $F(M\otimes GN)\xrightarrow{c}FM\otimes FGN\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_N}FM\otimes N$. The right tensor has the analogous comparison using $\epsilon_N\otimes1$. Consequently if tensor with $M$ is exact, so is tensor with $FM$, since composites of functors preserving finite limits and finite colimits preserve them, and preservation is invariant under natural isomorphism. Conversely apply the same argument to $G$ and use $GFM\cong M$ from the unit. This proves the flat-object equivalence, with both tensor orders agreeing through symmetry.

Suppose $P$ passes the acyclic tensor test in $\mathcal M$, and let $N$ be any acyclic complex of $\mathcal A$. Step 1 makes $G_{\rm Ch}N$ acyclic. There is a chain isomorphism
$$F_{\rm Ch}(P\otimes G_{\rm Ch}N)\xrightarrow{\tau}F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes F_{\rm Ch}G_{\rm Ch}N\xrightarrow{1\otimes\epsilon_N}F_{\rm Ch}P\otimes N.$$
Its source is acyclic by the test and step 1, so its target is acyclic. Conversely if $F_{\rm Ch}P$ passes the test, apply it to $F_{\rm Ch}A$ for any acyclic $A$ of $\mathcal M$. Step 4 identifies its tensor with $F_{\rm Ch}(P\otimes A)$, and step 1 reflects acyclicity. Thus $P\otimes A$ is acyclic for every such $A$. The signed swap of step 7 identifies the two tensor orders, so either acyclic-test convention gives the same condition. Apply this equivalence also to $G$, or use $FG\cong\mathrm{id}$, to get preservation and reflection for both functors.

In either category let $P$ pass the acyclic test and let $u:X\to Y$ be any quasi-isomorphism, without conditions on $X,Y$. By [lem-pur-quasi-iso-cone-acyclic], $C(u)$ is acyclic, hence $P\otimes C(u)$ is acyclic. The chain isomorphism supplied by [lem-sfb-additive-total-tensor-cone-comparison] identifies this tensor with $C(1_P\otimes u)$. Acyclicity is invariant under chain isomorphisms, so the same cone criterion shows that $1_P\otimes u$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Naturality of the Koszul braiding conjugates $u\otimes1_P$ to this map, so it is a quasi-isomorphism too. This proves both tests for arbitrary endpoints; no exactness of countable sums and no resolution theorem is used.

proof.text: Conversely let both tensor functors with $P$ preserve every quasi-isomorphism as in [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso]. For every acyclic $A$, the map $0\to A$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the definition of cohomology and quasi-isomorphism. Tensoring it gives $0\to P\otimes A$, since an additive tensor sends zero objects to zero objects. It is a quasi-isomorphism, so $P\otimes A$ is acyclic. Hence the two-sided quasi-isomorphism test and the acyclic test are equivalent in each category. Combining this with step 10 proves preservation and reflection of the two-sided test for $F_{\rm Ch}$ and $G_{\rm Ch}$, completing every asserted clause.
